answer: Picture three masks, Onyx, Juniper, and Canyon, one operator spins up to farm rewards. A shared-inference defense fingerprints each identity's answer-latency and traces its funding edges. Since all three run on one GPU pipeline, their replies land in the same serialized burst and their coins trace upstream to a single root like streams draining into a canyon, so the ledger collapses Onyx and Juniper into one share. To look independent the attacker must buy N parallel inference stacks and N separately funded, staggered wallets, pricing every extra mask at real hardware plus capital.
